items.text: Classification written on the job record before gear is ordered: emergency (700), legally required (701), or optional (702), with who required it.
Transfer equipment is listed for the use, and its marking matches the classification — emergency and legally required gear is marked for that use, and meter-mounted switches are not used there.
Manual transfer job: the intended-load list the owner selected is signed off in the job record, and the generator is sized to that list.
Automatic transfer job: load calculation (Article 220) or approved demand data is in the job record, and the design states full-load or load-management duty.
Load management, where claimed, is installed automatic equipment with its settings recorded — not an owner's promise to switch loads off.
Transfer equipment short-circuit rating meets the available fault current; on non-dwelling work the rating is field marked on the exterior of the gear.
No backfeed path exists in any switch position: utility and generator can never be interconnected, tested through every operation of the equipment.
Sign at the service (or at the dwelling emergency disconnect) gives the type and location of the standby source and its shutdown.
Power inlet sign matches the generator neutral: bonded (separately derived) only, or floating (nonseparately derived) only — verified against the actual generator.
Outdoor generator shutdown for the dwelling is in place outside at a readily accessible location, and nobody has confused it with the service emergency disconnect.

Outdoor set disconnect check: readily accessible and within sight of the building, or the portable set is 15 kW or less on a flanged inlet. Generator disconnect per 445.18; a disconnect where the supply conductors terminate in or on the building per 225.36.
New transfer gear furnished by Sharma is Siemens, per company standard.
If the standby work moved the meter or panel, the back-to-back layout and its working space were rechecked.
Portable-generator inlet rated 100 A or more: inlet equipment listed for the use and provided with an interlocked disconnecting means (702.12(C)), unless an exception applies.
Connection type decided and drawn: supply-side (705.11) or load-side (705.12), before any busbar math is quoted.
Each source lands on its own dedicated breaker or fusible disconnect; no source shares a breaker with a load or another source.
Busbar method named in the job record (100 percent, 120 percent, or sum-of-breakers) with the arithmetic shown, using 125 percent of source output current.
Under the 120 percent method the source breaker is at the opposite end of the bus from the main, and the do-not-relocate warning label is on the equipment beside it.
Multiple-source plaque or directory is installed at the service equipment showing every source disconnect location.
Power control system, where used, is listed, its controller setting is recorded in the job file, and access to the setting is controlled.
ESS disconnect is readily accessible (outside the dwelling or its remote control is), shows open/closed, and is marked as the energy storage system disconnect with its voltage and fault-current data.
Existing panel on an interconnection job keeps breakers listed for that panel — no mixed brands to satisfy the math.
